mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a labor market so tight that wage inflation will soon accelerate, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPI inflation falls more than 0.5pp in the month following the signal, indicating that the Fed will not need to tighten policy aggressively.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a supply crunch that will drive up costs and erode corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: ISM Manufacturing PMI rises above 60 in the month following the signal, indicating that the supply chain pressures are easing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed cuts rates by more than 50bps in an emergency inter-meeting move within 2 weeks of the signal, indicating a policy pivot.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts growth accelerates by more than 20% year-over-year, it signals over-exuberance in the housing market that will soon reverse, leading to a slowdown in a key sector and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates fall by more than 50bps in the month following the signal, indicating that housing affordability is improving.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market slowdown that will depress consumer spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fall by more than 20,000 per week in the week following the signal, indicating that the labor market is not as weak as the payroll data suggest.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals a consumer spending slowdown that will depress corporate earnings and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises by more than 5 points in the month following the signal, indicating that the spending slowdown is likely to be temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate rises above 3% and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals that the Fed is behind the curve on inflation and will need to raise rates aggressively, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed raises rates by more than 50bps at the next FOMC meeting following the signal, indicating that they are catching up to the inflation problem.
